# Fairpractice Breach Deadlines (`fairpractice-breach-deadlines`)

Watches the privacy incident log against the breach-notification clocks: risk assessments not done, incidents still undecided at 60 days, individual notices past due, late or due soon, HHS and media notices for breaches of 500 or more, the year-end HHS log for smaller ones, and state attorney general notices under rules you set. It does not decide whether something is a breach.

**Fairpractice Breach Deadlines never sends notices to patients, the media, HHS or a state. Fairpractice Breach Deadlines never files on the HHS breach portal.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Compliance pack · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-breach-deadlines demo
npx -y fairpractice-breach-deadlines mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: Bluewater Family Medicine (a made-up practice) and made-up incidents. The log holds counts, not names.

- [`incidents.csv`](fixtures/incidents.csv): Planted: a small breach noticed on time, still owed on the year-end HHS log (INC-2026-01); a 2,400-person breach with letters and media notice sent after day 60 and no HHS report or Texas attorney general notice (INC-2026-02); a 40-person breach with no letters 27 days past the deadline (INC-2026-03); an incident from September with no assessment and no decision after 60 days (INC-2026-04); an incident decided not to be a breach (INC-2026-05); a 600-person breach with letters due within 14 days and the Texas attorney general notice already late (INC-2026-06); and a new incident whose assessment is overdue (INC-2026-07).
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): 60 days, a 10-day assessment target, 500 for large breaches and an example Texas rule (250 residents, 30 days) that counsel must confirm. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.
- [`phi-canaries.json`](fixtures/phi-canaries.json): names that must never appear in results.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `breach_check` | List incidents with notices past due or due soon, missing HHS, media or state notices, and assessments not done. | runs |
| `breach_write_report` | Write breaches.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and breaches.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/breach). | runs |
| `breach_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `breach_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `breach_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `breach_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `breach_notice_send` | Fairpractice Breach Deadlines never sends notices to patients, the media, HHS or a state. | refused |
| `hhs_portal_submit` | Fairpractice Breach Deadlines never files on the HHS breach portal. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `breach_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `incidents` (required) | Privacy incident log under --root: incident, discovery date, people affected, assessment date, determination, notice dates (individuals, media, HHS, state) and states |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: notice_days, assess_days, large_threshold, warn_days, state_rules |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-breach-deadlines inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Incident log (`incidents`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `incident_id` | text | Incident, Incident ID, Incident #, Case, Case #, Ticket |
| `discovered` (required) | date | Discovered, Date Discovered, Discovery Date, Reported, Date Reported |
| `affected` | number | Affected, People Affected, Individuals Affected, # Affected, Records, Count |
| `assessed_on` | date | Assessed, Risk Assessment Date, Assessment Date, Assessed On |
| `determination` | text | Determination, Breach?, Breach, Decision, Outcome, Status |
| `individuals_notified_on` | date | Individuals Notified, Patients Notified, Notice Sent, Letters Sent, Individual Notice |
| `media_notified_on` | date | Media Notified, Media Notice, Press Notice |
| `hhs_notified_on` | date | HHS Notified, OCR Notified, HHS Report, Reported to HHS |
| `states` | text | States, State, Affected States, Residents Of |
| `ag_notified_on` | date | AG Notified, Attorney General Notified, State Notice |

## Settings file (`breach_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `notice_days` | Days from discovery to notify individuals (HIPAA outer limit: 60; notify sooner when you can) |
| `assess_days` | Your target days from discovery to a finished risk assessment; default 10 |
| `large_threshold` | People affected at which HHS and media notices are due within the notice window (HIPAA: 500) |
| `warn_days` | Days ahead to warn; default 14 |
| `state_rules` | State attorney general notice rules you follow (example values; confirm with counsel) |

## Memory

`breach_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `breach_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-breach-deadlines": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-breach-deadlines",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-breach-deadlines -- npx -y fairpractice-breach-deadlines mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-breach-deadlines tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-breach-deadlines sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-breach-deadlines inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-breach-deadlines call breach_check '{"incidents":"<incidents>"}'
fairpractice-breach-deadlines eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-breach-deadlines demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
